_comment: signal_modulation/design01 — Nd:YAG crystal as a pump-controlled signal modulator: CW 1064 nm signal through a side-pumped (808 nm, from above) crystal; the pump sets the inversion, the inversion sets the gain the signal sees. Design 01 starts PRE-INVERTED (see sted) — physically right, since the 230 us storage time means the crystal is simply full when the signal arrives; the pump's job is refilling burned inversion, not building it. modulating the pump to imprint a signal comes in design 02. REALISM NOTES: wavelengths, level structure (4-level: 808 absorb 4I9/2->4F5/2, fast decay to 4F3/2, 1064 emit 4F3/2->4I11/2, fast decay to ground) and the LINEWIDTHS are real Nd:YAG (gammaE 5.3e-4 = 159 GHz, gammaA 1.5e-3 = 459 GHz in MEEP units — 190x narrower than the dyes we've used; consequence: polarization ringdown ~600 t.u., so run_until must be a few thousand, and the modulation ceiling is the 159 GHz gain bandwidth = nothing faster than ~6 ps imprints). The DOPING is deliberately scaled: literal 1 at.% Nd (sigma_em 2.8e-19 cm2, N 1.38e20 /cm3) gives gL = 0.077 over 20 um — invisible. SGMA*N here is chosen ~30x that so single-pass gain is O(10): equivalent to a highly-doped numerical crystal, same line shapes. Lifetimes NOT literal either: real tau(4F3/2) = 230 us = 7e10 t.u. can never reach steady state in-sim; rate_43/rate_21 keep the dye-model convention (fast feeder/drain), and the upper level effectively does not decay over the run — which is the correct 230-us-limit behaviour at these timescales. YAG n = 1.82; background 1.77 = weak guiding with 0.02% facet reflection (real YAG-in-air facets are 8% and would make a cavity — that is a DIFFERENT experiment, do it deliberately or not at all). SGMA/pump amplitude need the usual first-run calibration sweep. Created 2026-09-01.

crystal._comment: the Nd:YAG block. sted = the same 4-level Maxwell-Bloch machinery as the dyes, with Nd:YAG's lines: lbdA 0.808, lbdE 1.064, REAL linewidths. SGMA x N is the scaled doping (see top comment).

sted._comment: 4-level Nd:YAG START­ING FULLY INVERTED (N3_0=30, N1_0=0, user 2026-09-01): the 230 us upper-level lifetime means a pre-pumped crystal simply IS in this state when the signal arrives — no in-sim buildup needed. The CW pump then only REFILLS what stimulated emission burns (gain recovery), which is the dynamics that matters for modulation.

source_1._comment: CW 1064 nm signal, Ey, guided in from the left.

source_pump._comment: 808 nm CW pump entering the crystal FROM ABOVE: y-normal sheet on the crystal's top edge radiating down (SimpleSim free source placement, 2026-09-01). Ez, orthogonal to the Ey signal, so they never interfere directly; the crystal is isotropic so the pump still drives 1->4.

snap_point._comment: single-point time trace at the chain's exit — the settling diagnostic: steady state is reached when this envelope flattens. dt 0.2 = 17 samples per 1064 nm optical period.

pop_monitor._comment: Level populations N_l(t) AVERAGED over the crystal — the modulator's own state variable, and the cleanest read of when emission balances refill (N3 flattens). NOTE: no snap_interval on purpose. With snap_interval > 0 this sensor also stores the whole-cell snap_N (n_snaps, n_levels, Nx, Ny) + snap_E, which at 6000 t.u. is GBs per task; without it save() writes only {t, N}, the summed per-level series (sensor.py:305).
